chapter: Tick Chambers and the Dodds brothers
title: Trumpeter Tick Chambers and Jimmy Strokes
summary: Allen asks about Tick Chambers, who never recorded; Robichaux calls him and Jimmy Strokes good, popular New Orleans trumpeters who went to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Remembering King Oliver: the man, the band, the decline

blocks.x: Speaking of trumpet players, I was going to ask you about Tick Chambers because I never knew anything about him.
He was another good trumpet player. Now that was another trumpet player that you don't hear much about.
He never made any records, so nobody knows about him.

He never made any records, but he was a good trumpet player, and he was quite popular around New Orleans, too, before he left, went to Chicago. Him and Tick Chambers both. Tick Chambers, I meant to say, Jimmy Strokes was another good trumpet player he was from New Orleans.
So how did Tick get played? Was he a high note man?
